planned_title: If You Can't See the Nearest Star, How Far Away Is It?
replaces_for_review: mon16_cant_see_nearest_star_v01/v02 (scheduled HZGTovJu_TQ). Earlier versions not overwritten.
spoken: The nearest star to the Sun You can't see it. It's called Proxima Centauri, a small red dwarf. It gives out less than 1% of the Sun's light. Hold up your thumb at arm's length. Close one eye, then the other. Your thumb jumps against the background. Your two eyes are a ruler. Astronomers use the same trick with the whole of Earth's orbit. Its light still takes more than four years to reach you.
